register.name: Bhutan Livable and Resilient Cities Project (FP315)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 27 October 2026 (Board meeting B.46) · loan $5.6 million and grant $22.4 million · total value $48 million · accredited entity: the World Bank (IBRD and IDA)
register.note: Co-financing of $20 million, half loan and half grant; about 376,000 people expected to gain resilience
register.text: Green Climate Fund financing for resilient cities, with the World Bank as accredited entity. It is to climate-proof the water system, create a ring-fenced water services division within Thimphu Thromde and build Bhutan’s first bus priority system, an 18.9-kilometre corridor served by 50 battery electric buses. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Gamri-II 55 MW Hydropower Project
register.detail: OPEC Fund · approved 11 December 2025 · loan agreement signed in Vienna, 24 June 2026 · total project cost $61.76 million · executing agency DGPC
register.note: Signed on the same day as a Framework Agreement for Private Sector Operations between Bhutan and the OPEC Fund
register.text: An OPEC Fund loan to the Royal Government of Bhutan for a 55 MW run-of-river hydropower plant, with Druk Green Power Corporation as executing agency. It adds clean generation to the grid and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Dorjilung Hydroelectric Power Project
register.detail: World Bank · Boards approved 22 January 2026 · IDA $300 million ($150 million grant, $150 million credit) and IBRD $215 million, signed 5 May 2026 · 1,125 MW · estimated cost $1.7 billion
register.note: Project company owned 60% by Druk Green Power Corporation and 40% by Tata Power; IFC adds up to $300 million (separate line)
register.text: World Bank financing for the 1,125 MW Dorjilung hydropower plant, an estimated $1.7 billion public-private partnership that is to generate more than 4,500 GWh of clean electricity a year. It is designed to close the winter energy gap at home and export surplus summer power to India, and serves the energy standard.

register.name: First Growth and Jobs Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank · approved 1 April 2026 · $12.5 million grant and $12.5 million concessional financing (40 years, 10 years’ grace) · first in a series of three
register.note: Reforms to tax, foreign investment, external commercial borrowing, public investment, pensions and farmer cooperatives
register.text: Budget support from the World Bank, half grant and half concessional financing, for reforms that aim to create jobs. It backs fiscal and debt management, a modernised tax system, a better framework for foreign investment, stronger farmer cooperatives and better working conditions for women, youth and vulnerable groups. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Accelerate Bhutan’s Job Transformation through Renewable Natural Resource Value Chains Project
register.detail: World Bank · Board approved 12 June 2025 · $29.8 million IDA financing and $4.7 million PROGREEN grant
register.note: About 42,000 people expected to benefit, 65 percent of them women
register.text: World Bank financing for high-potential farm value chains such as dairy, citrus and potato, to create jobs in renewable natural resources. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Climate and Disaster Resilience DPF with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Program Document of 12 November 2024 · approved 11 December 2024 · IDA credit $20 million and IDA grant $20 million
register.note: A Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option within the operation; no separate drawdown amount is stated
register.text: Budget support with a contingent credit line that can be drawn when disaster strikes. It backs reforms that integrate climate and disaster resilience into critical infrastructure and buildings and strengthen natural disaster early warning and the financial resilience of property. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Second Green and Resilient Growth DPC
register.note: A development policy credit: budget support tied to policy reforms
register.text: Budget support from the World Bank for policies that strengthen private sector-led growth through fiscal sustainability and better access to finance and markets, and that promote green growth in renewable natural resources. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Enhancing Resilience with Countercyclical Expenditures Program
register.detail: ADB · approved 23 October 2026 · $13.45 million Asian Development Fund grant and $3.97 million ordinary capital resources loan
register.note: Supports the Government’s $267.88 million Anti-Crisis Action Plan
register.text: ADB support to protect vulnerable families from rising food and energy costs, in response to the impacts of the Middle East conflict. It backs the Government’s Anti-Crisis Action Plan, which includes monthly assistance of up to 10,000 ngultrum for women in eligible large families, energy bill subsidies for rural households, expanded school feeding and tax exemptions on basic foods. It serves the food, energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Solar Farm Expansion Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 30 June 2026 · signed 31 July 2026 · ordinary capital resources loan $160 million, with a $0.5 million grant · at least 310 MW
register.note: Signing announced by the Ministry of Finance, 31 July 2026; expected to catalyse about $68.7 million of private equity and commercial debt
register.text: An ADB loan for at least 310 MW of new solar generation in three solar farm subprojects, one of them a public-private partnership; the loan finances most expenditures, including Druk Green Power Corporation’s equity in the joint venture. It adds solar power to Bhutan’s grid and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Inclusive and Resilient Urban Development Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 27 June 2026 · signed 31 July 2026 · $5 million concessional loan, $5 million Asian Development Fund grant and $3 million Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific grant
register.note: Signing announced by the Ministry of Finance, 31 July 2026; at least 30% of the affordable homes for women-headed households
register.text: ADB financing for drainage, water supply, sewerage, roads, walkways and flood protection in the Ammochhu local area of Phuentsholing, and 56 affordable rental homes for vulnerable households in Thimphu and Phuentsholing. It serves shelter, the standard furthest from reach, and water.

register.name: Trade Expansion and Diversification Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: ADB · approved 10 February 2026 · $13 million policy-based loan and $12 million Asian Development Fund grant · Loan 4752-BHU, agreement document of 12 February 2026
register.note: The loan is from ADB’s concessional ordinary operations
register.text: Policy-based ADB financing for legal, regulatory, procedural and institutional reforms to strengthen Bhutan’s trade ecosystem, export competitiveness and market access for Bhutanese enterprises. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Strengthening the Banking and Capital Markets Reforms Program
register.detail: ADB · approved 9 December 2025 · $10 million policy-based loan and $5 million policy-based grant
register.note: Includes credit rating agencies and a national framework for green and social bonds
register.text: Policy-based ADB financing to strengthen the banking and capital markets and enhance financial inclusion. Planned reforms include stabilising banks, setting up credit rating agencies and creating a national framework for green and social bonds, a possible new channel of finance for the seven standards.

register.name: Distributed Solar for Public Infrastructure Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 23 September 2024 · Loan 4491-BHU signed 24 September 2024 · concessional ordinary capital resources loan · total cost $34 million
register.note: Up to 35 MW of solar systems on rooftops of public infrastructure; a $1 million technical assistance grant alongside
register.text: An ADB loan for solar power systems on public buildings and land across the country, up to 35 MW, to increase non-hydro clean power and build skills for green jobs. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Concessional Line of Credit for energy projects
register.detail: Government of India · announced at the State Visit of 11 and 12 November 2025 · INR 40 billion (Rs 4,000 crore)
register.note: News reports (PTI, 31 July 2026) state that the agreement was signed in Thimphu; no government page on the signing was opened
register.text: A concessional line of credit from India to fund energy projects in Bhutan, announced in the joint press release on the State Visit of the Prime Minister of India. It serves the energy standard, alongside India’s commitment of INR 10,000 crore to Bhutan’s 13th Five Year Plan (July 2024 to June 2029).

register.name: Support for Bhutan’s 13th Five Year Plan
register.detail: Government of India · plan period July 2024 to June 2029 · as stated by the Ministry of External Affairs, June 2026
register.note: Stated in the Ministry of External Affairs brief on India–Bhutan relations, June 2026
register.text: The Government of India’s commitment of support for Bhutan’s 13th Five Year Plan period, July 2024 to June 2029. The plan finances public services and investments behind the seven standards.

register.name: Dorjilung Hydroelectric Power Project: IFC A loan
register.detail: IFC · approved by the World Bank Group Boards 22 January 2026 · A loan to Dorjilung Hydro Power Limited, alongside a $200 million IBRD enclave loan
register.note: Project company owned 60% by Druk Green Power Corporation and 40% by Tata Power; signing of the IFC loan not stated
register.text: An IFC loan to the company building the 1,125 MW Dorjilung plant, part of a World Bank Group package of $815 million that is to mobilise about $900 million from private investors. It brings private capital to the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Every unit of power from rivers that fall from the Himalaya.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Forest across seven tenths of the land, protected by law and by custom.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Almost 100,000 cubic metres of fresh water a person each year: among the richest endowments on earth.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Monasteries, mountains and a policy of high-value, low-volume tourism.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 20.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Tarayana Foundation
items.text: A Bhutanese foundation whose flagship housing improvement programme had facilitated the construction of 2,652 houses for vulnerable rural families by April 2024. Its integrated community development services, specialising in housing, received a World Habitat Silver Award in 2021.

items.name: Bhutan Toilet Organisation
items.text: Founded by Passang Tshering, it works for safe and hygienic toilets across the country, from remote schools to busy highways. Under its founder’s Jinpa Toilet initiative, 14 businesses had opened their toilets to the public by September 2025.

items.name: Soyalla
items.text: A social enterprise launched in 2022 to tackle Bhutan’s nutritional and economic challenges. It produces flavoured soy milks, fresh and frozen tofu and soy sprinkles, from soybeans sourced from six dzongkhags (2025).

items.name: Mountain Hazelnuts
items.text: Bhutan’s leading forest-based agribusiness, based in Lingmethang, which works with thousands of rural hazelnut growers across the country (2025).
